thread:
rachel: FYI customer Julie (acct: cust_9f1e) opened INC-4523 — their March invoice shows ~2.1M billed tokens but the console shows ~1.3M served tokens. They mention continuous batching + kv-prefetch. Logs attached.

kevin: Can you paste the customer id, model, and whether they're on Hosted/Dedicated?

rachel: Hosted, plan=standard, customer_id=cust_9f1e, model=gpt-4o-compat, sample headers:
```
X-Customer-ID: cust_9f1e
X-Request-ID: req_0a9c7f
x-prefetch: true
continuous_batching_window_ms: 100
```

maya: thx. I'll run a metering query across the period — we should compare billed_tokens vs served_tokens grouped by request_id and batch_window.

metering-bot: metering ingestion lag: 0.8% for selected timeframe. Note: prefetch events are emitted at request arrival as 'prefetch_billed' metric.

sam: My hunch: prefetch/KV warmup does token accounting at request time for the full prefetched prefix. If continuous batching later dedupes/merges tokens across requests, those prefetched tokens may never be 'served' but were billed. Cold-start warmups amplify this.

kevin: can we get an example request_id + logs from invoice time? need to trace metering record -> serving event.

rachel: here's req_0a9c7f log excerpt:
```
[2026-03-10T12:03:05Z] req=req_0a9c7f prefetched_prefix=153 tokens billed_prefetch=true cache_hit=false batch_id=bay-42
[2026-03-10T12:03:05Z] req=req_0a9c7f served_tokens=42
```

maya: ran quick query:
```
SELECT request_id, sum(billed_tokens) AS billed, sum(served_tokens) AS served
FROM metering.events
WHERE customer_id='cust_9f1e' AND ts BETWEEN '2026-03-01' AND '2026-03-11'
GROUP BY request_id
ORDER BY billed-served DESC
LIMIT 5;
```
results: many rows where billed - served ~100-200 tokens; top aggregate delta ~800k tokens across month.

rachel: customer asked if this is a bug or expected. They want a short explainer + whether we can credit the difference.

kevin: propose: (1) explain cause (prefetch counted when requested, serving dedup later), (2) offer one-time credit covering the measured delta after we verify patterns, (3) apply mitigation: reduce their continuous_batching_window_ms to 0 or disable kv-prefetch while we investigate.

sam: quick mitigation command (on route config):
```
redwoodctl routes update --customer cust_9f1e \
  --set continuous_batching_window_ms=0 \
  --set kv_prefetch=false
```
This will stop prefetch-warmups being billed aggressively.

rachel: i'll propose a 30% credit initially and enable the mitigation. please create an internal Jira for deeper analysis.

jira-bot: Created BILL-789 "prefetch billing delta investigation" and linked this thread.

kevin: assign to maya + sam. maya, can you run a full audit and dump the per-day deltas? Sam, please add an insertion to the billing runbook about prefetch behavior.

maya: will do, starting the audit now. ETA EOD.

rachel: thanks team :heart: i'll update customer that we found a pattern, offering credits and immediate mitigation.
